questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
The university website was easy to navigate and it was easy to find the courses for the semester
The university also had to be located close to nature and not in a bigger city, as I study environmental science

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Check in to my apartment and information on resources at the university campus and at the student accommodation

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Apartments shared with 5 others and private rooms with shared bathrooms.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: As I lived in my own apartment with 5 others, we had a huge kitchen. I am aware that other students had common kitchens to cook in.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: The apartments at 20 College Rd belonging to Fischer College are amazing! Unfortunately, I have been informed, that UTAS is planning to close down the Sandy Bay Campus, which would make the accommodation at 20 College Rd useless as all the students would then be far away from city campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Georgia, the incoming exchange coordinator, was always very helpful. She helped me change courses during the first few weeks. The online portals were also easy for registration.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Georgia was always available!

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesfull

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
To not stress about choosing the wrong classes as you can change within the first week if you're not happy.
To check where the classes are located, as there are different campuses and your classes might be overlapping, which is not good, if you need to transport yourself between the campuses

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was not satisfied with all the online classes.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took 3 courses in which both masters and bachelors students attended. I however was enrolled in the BA courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
I prefer UCPH, as UCPH has a clear reading plan (they tell you which books you need to read). At UTAS there was not any required reading other than notes, that the teachers had written. There was a lot of supplied online content of bad quality and it was confusing (for some courses) to figure out where to find the content and what you actually had to learn. The level of teaching was not as high as at UCPH. 
However, I definitely did learn something, but it was a different experience. I did like that 3 of my courses included a lot of field trips.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Plant Pathology
Microbiology
Agricultural Landscape Systems
Agricultural Technology and Innovation

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend Agricultural Landscape Systems and Agricultural Technology and Innovation, as they touch on important knowledge. However, both courses were not of the highest quality.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Many different sports events and parties (mostly suitable for 18 year old Aussie students or young exchange students though)

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Attending the gym or uni-sports clubs

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Cradle Mountain, Coles Bay (Freycinet Nationalpark), Tasman Peninsula, MONA museum, Salamance Market (every Saturday), Tallows Beach, go on weekend trips or when you have a holiday, rent a car and go around Tasmania!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Attend the social events - especially the first 1-2 weeks! And get there a while before the semester starts.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That Aussies love being outside hiking, surfing, socialising in cafes

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Be aware that other exchange students and locals are very young between 18-21 years (I myself am nearly 27 yo)
- Make sure you have a drivers license, so you can go explore Tasmania on the weekends

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Nothing

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Making 5 new Danish friends in my apartment and the lovely nature of Tasmania

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Nothing

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
